questions.stem: Solution A has a pH of 2 and Solution B has a pH of 4. How do the hydrogen ion concentrations compare?

options.text: Solution A has twice the H+ concentration of Solution B
Solution A has 100 times the H+ concentration of Solution B
Solution B has 100 times the H+ concentration of Solution A
Both solutions have the same H+ concentration

questions.explanation: The pH scale is logarithmic. Each decrease of 1 pH unit represents a 10-fold increase in H+ concentration. A difference of 2 pH units means 10 x 10 = 100 times more H+ ions. Solution A (pH 2) has 100 times more H+ ions per unit volume than Solution B (pH 4).

questions.stem: A student measures the pH of pure water as 7. She then dissolves a small amount of sodium chloride in the water. What pH would she expect?

options.text: Below 7, because salts are acidic
Above 7, because sodium is a metal
Still 7, because sodium chloride is a neutral salt
Exactly 14, because NaCl is alkaline

questions.explanation: Sodium chloride is formed from a strong acid (HCl) and a strong alkali (NaOH). When dissolved in water, it produces a neutral solution with pH 7. The Na+ and Cl- ions do not affect the H+ or OH- concentrations in the water. Not all salts are neutral, but NaCl is.

questions.stem: A student gradually adds sodium hydroxide solution to hydrochloric acid while monitoring the pH. The pH starts at 1. What happens to the pH during the addition?

options.text: pH stays at 1 throughout
pH gradually increases from 1, passes through 7 at neutralisation, and continues above 7 with excess alkali
pH jumps directly from 1 to 14
pH decreases from 1 to 0

questions.explanation: As NaOH is added, it neutralises the HCl, removing H+ ions. The pH gradually rises. At the exact point of neutralisation, pH = 7 (strong acid + strong alkali). If more NaOH is added beyond this point, excess OH- ions make the solution alkaline and the pH continues to rise above 7.

questions.stem: Lemon juice has a pH of about 2, and black coffee has a pH of about 5. Which substance is more acidic and by approximately how much?

options.text: Lemon juice is 3 times more acidic
Black coffee is 3 times more acidic
Lemon juice is about 1000 times more acidic
They are equally acidic

questions.explanation: The pH scale is logarithmic. A difference of 3 pH units (5 - 2 = 3) means 10^3 = 1000 times more H+ ions. Lemon juice (pH 2) has about 1000 times the concentration of H+ ions compared to coffee (pH 5), making it about 1000 times more acidic.

questions.stem: A student uses a pH meter and finds that oven cleaner has a pH of 13.5. What does this tell us about the solution?

options.text: It is a strong acid
It is neutral
It is a strongly alkaline solution with a very high concentration of OH- ions
It is a weak acid

questions.explanation: A pH of 13.5 is very close to 14, indicating a strongly alkaline solution. It has a very high concentration of OH- ions and a very low concentration of H+ ions. Oven cleaners typically contain sodium hydroxide (NaOH), a strong alkali. Such solutions are very corrosive and must be handled with care.
